title: Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy Hospitalized After Suffering Stroke
snippet: U.S. Sen. Chris Murphy of Connecticut was hospitalized after suffering a stroke over the weekend. Aides report the lawmaker is awake, alert, and expected to make a full recovery.
content:
U.S. Sen. Chris Murphy has been hospitalized after suffering a stroke over the weekend, his office announced Sunday. The 53-year-old Connecticut Democrat was transferred to Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore, where medical staff remain optimistic about his prognosis.

According to his chief of staff, Allison Herwitt, Murphy began experiencing numbness in his arm on Saturday while attending his son's hockey game. Subsequent medical evaluations confirmed that he had suffered a stroke.

Doctors Express Optimism

"The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery," Herwitt said in a statement. No additional details regarding his current condition or treatment timeline have been released.

The unexpected health scare comes in the final stretch of the midterm election cycle. Murphy had spent recent weeks traveling across the country to campaign on behalf of Democratic candidates, including a scheduled appearance Sunday in New Hampshire alongside Democratic Senate candidate Chris Pappas.

Support Rolls In from Connecticut Leaders

First elected to the Senate in 2012, Murphy secured his third term representing Connecticut in 2024 and has frequently been discussed by Democratic insiders as a prospective presidential candidate for 2028.

Following the announcement, Connecticut Governor Ned Lamont offered his support, noting he had recently joined Murphy on the campaign trail.

"Just two days ago, I was with Senator Chris Murphy doing what he loves most: encouraging Connecticut residents to make their voices heard," Lamont shared on social media. "There is no stronger advocate for our democracy. And no one who fights harder for the people of this state. Chris is a great friend to Connecticut and to me personally."
